turns.en: People just run like they have to use online productivity software, collaboration tools.
turns.zh: 人们就像在拼命使用在线生产力软件和协作工具一样。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: Yeah, blessing and a curse. Speaking of a blessing and curse, this is a great segue to where I wanted to go in the final area I want to spend time on which is building horizontal software and building software that bundles together a bunch of different stuff. Notoriously hard to build a horizontal platform that does a lot of things when there are often point solutions that are very, very good at that one thing. And it's interesting. If you look at the timelines of companies that have built horizontal products, they all take a long time to build and finally find product market fits. It's actually a really common pattern. And when we were talking about what would be fun to talk about, the way you described it is the joy and pain of building horizontal products. So let me just ask broadly just what have you learned about what it takes to successfully build a horizontal platform type of product?
turns.zh: 是啊，这真是喜忧参半。说到喜忧参半，这正好引出我接下来想谈的重点——构建横向软件和整合多种功能的软件平台。开发一个能处理多种业务的横向平台通常困难重重，因为市面上往往有针对单一场景的专有解决方案，而且这些方案在各自领域都做得极其出色。很有意思的是，那些开发横向产品的公司在产品线规划上往往耗时良久，最终才找到产品与市场的契合点。这其实是一个很常见的模式。当我们讨论横向产品开发的乐趣与挑战时，你提到横向产品开发的痛点和机遇。那么，我想问问大家，成功打造横向平台产品需要具备哪些要素？

turns.speaker: Ivan Zhao
turns.en: First of all, no regret. And second, I wouldn't want to build anything else because going back to the value, Lego for software doesn't exist and Lego is a horizontal thing. So that's the thing we want to build. We always want to do that. So we did not start to optimize for business but we're optimized for that vision. (00:52:19): Learning-wise, I think segmentation is quite important because people can use a Lego for different things. Only hardcore Lego fans care about Lego bricks. Most people care about Lego boxes. And they actually want the Lego box to be ready-made. When you unpack the box, the set is there for you, right? That's what we're learning a lot, especially move up market. There's this term that took me a while to learn. It's called solutions. You need to be a solution for enterprise customer, you need to sit somewhere on a P&L to optimize for their business where due third risk. That's Lego box. It's not a Lego brick. Segmentation related to that. So you need to shift your mindset as you more towards B2B, more towards move out market. I wish we have done earlier. For the longest time, I've stalled too much in the Lego brick mindset, now in the solution Lego box mindset.
turns.zh: 首先，没有遗憾。其次，我不想开发其他类型的产品，因为从价值角度来看，软件领域不存在“乐高积木”式的横向产品，而乐高本身就是横向整合的典范。所以这正是我们想要打造的。我们始终致力于此。最初，我们并非为了商业效益而优化产品，而是为了实现愿景而优化。（00:52:19）：在学习方面，我认为细分市场至关重要，因为人们可以将乐高积木用于不同场景。只有铁杆乐高迷才会关注积木块，大多数人关注的是乐高套装。人们希望套装能直接使用，打开包装后就能直接玩。这正是我们在高端市场中领悟到的经验。有一个词汇让我花了些时间才理解——“解决方案”。你需要为企业客户提供解决方案，需要融入企业的损益表，优化其业务流程，承担第三方风险。这就是乐高套装，而非积木块。这与细分市场息息相关。因此，当你向B2B市场转型、开拓高端市场时，思维模式需要转变。真希望我们能早点意识到这一点。在很长一段时间里，我深陷于乐高积木式的思维模式，如今才转向解决方案式、乐高套装式的思维模式。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: That's such a good metaphor. I feel like even if you're not building Legos for business, just this idea of what is the box that you are selling to people, how's it being positioned? How do you picture it? What are the value? Props such a good metaphor.
turns.zh: 这个比喻太妙了。即便你不为商业打造乐高产品，思考如何向用户销售套装、如何定位产品、如何构想价值，这本身也是很有启发的。这个比喻太棒了。

turns.speaker: Ivan Zhao
turns.en: If you're building vertical software and naturally your vertical is the box, right? So you know you have 1 or 2% of your selling to. Pretty straightforward that your market constrains you and no judgment. People like you, you can go that way, but then you just hit the wall off the market. The advantage of building horizontal, there's no wall, at least for in our space. We, Notion, go after entire software market, but then you need to create a wall yourself. So to make your go-to-market distribution, to create the spot in people's mind, your customer's mind more clearly for them and for your go-to-market teams. That's why where solutions is one of my favorite word internally to rally the sales team or the product team. You think that way, but then you need to hold in your head, make sure you're still building bricks behind the scene. Otherwise, you pigeonhole yourself into the best spot, like what we did with project management sprints features.
turns.zh: 假设你正在开发垂直软件，显然你的垂直领域是项目管理，对吧？所以你知道你的目标客户只有1%到2%。很显然，市场会限制你的发展空间，这没什么可指责的。如果你认同这种思路，可以沿着这条路走，但最终你会撞上市场天花板。开发横向软件的好处在于没有这种限制——至少在我们所在的领域是这样。我们Notion的目标是整个软件市场，但你需要自己去构建市场壁垒。为了让你的市场推广更清晰，在用户和销售团队心中占据一席之地，这就是为什么“解决方案”是我公司内部最常用来激励销售团队或产品团队的口号。这种思维很重要，但同时你要确保在幕后持续打磨产品，否则你就会把自己局限在一个最佳位置，就像我们在项目管理冲刺功能上所做的那样。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: So speaking of that, so I don't know if you know this. I ran a survey recently where I asked my readers what tools they use most, what tools they love most. And it went out to my entire subscriber base. We've got 6,500 people filling out the survey. And Notion more than any other company placed very highly in many categories. For example, I have the notes here, it was the second most popular project management tool after Jira. It was the fourth most popular docs. Which is interesting because you think Notion would... Notion is known for docs and it's interesting, that was the lowest one actually. And then it was third in CRM, just behind Salesforce and HubSpot.
turns.zh: 说到这，我不知道你是否了解。最近我做了一项调查，向读者询问他们最常使用的工具和最喜欢的工具。调查覆盖了我的全部订阅用户群体，共有6,500人参与。Notion在多个类别中表现出色。比如这里我有笔记数据，Notion是仅次于Jira的第二受欢迎的项目管理工具，也是第四受欢迎的文档管理工具。这很有趣，因为大家普遍认为Notion以文档管理见长，但实际上在文档管理方面排名最低。然后在CRM领域，Notion位列第三，仅次于Salesforce和HubSpot。

turns.speaker: Ivan Zhao
turns.en: Yeah, we did not intend to build CRM, but what is a CRM is relational database. That's why we give people that brick. That's a relational database and they can build CRM themselves. I think the good advantage is if a customer use Notion, they can address those three, four use cases in one place. Especially for our startup mid-market companies, their need for each of the vertical use case is not as complex so they can have all the information in one place, good for their teams, good for AI actually. That's a huge market change that's like we did not expect until recently. And save their costs, which is more and more people care about the bundling purchase nowadays. And our approach for that is, yes, we're number two in project management, number what? Number four in CRM, but we're interested in more bricks to make us number... Move up the categories in ranking. So it just takes time, but that's our approach.
turns.zh: 是的，我们原本无意开发CRM，但CRM本质上就是关系型数据库。这就是为什么我们为用户提供了基础模块——关系型数据库，让他们可以自行搭建CRM系统。我认为最大的优势在于，如果客户使用Notion，他们可以在一个平台上解决这三到四个使用场景。这对我们的初创企业和中型市场客户尤其有益，他们对垂直用例的需求没那么复杂，因此能将所有信息整合在一个地方，对团队和AI都很有益。这是我们未曾预料到的巨大市场变化。同时，节省成本也越来越受到关注，如今越来越多人青睐捆绑式购买。我们采取的策略是，在项目管理领域排名第二，在CRM领域排名第四，但我们致力于通过不断积累，提升各领域的排名。这需要时间，但这就是我们的策略。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: Yeah. Well, it's working whatever you're doing there. So say someone is trying to build a horizontal tool like yours. There's a lot of founders that are trying to build something that can do a lot of things really well. Do you have any advice for that first use case? Just figuring out something that initially works like you're talking about segmentation, is there something there of like, "Do this if you want to find any success with a horizontal tool"?
turns.zh: 是啊，无论你怎么做都很成功。假设有人想开发像你们这样的横向工具。很多创业者都试图打造一款能出色完成多项任务的产品。对于首个使用场景，你有什么建议吗？比如像你提到的细分市场策略，有没有什么通用法则，比如“如果想让横向工具成功，就必须这样做”之类的？

turns.speaker: Ivan Zhao
turns.en: First, I wouldn't recommend it.
turns.zh: 首先，我不建议这么做。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: But you wouldn't do it differently?
turns.zh: 但你不会采取不同的策略吗？

turns.speaker: Ivan Zhao
turns.en: I wouldn't do it differently myself, but I wouldn't recommend it. It's a problem. The problem space too large to have best practice, but I can share something that's relevant for us. Notion, we always want to build a meta tool, a tool to build the lack of our software. We somehow stand up upon document notes as one use case. And that just gave us a large top of the funnel that there's a 1 billion plus people use this use case every day. So that fuels our growth. We call our internal strategy called B2C2B. All those consumers, personal user use Notion for the most simple way you can use a computer or your phone, which is note-taking or document-sharing. And then they realize, "Oh, Notion can do more of that." There's relational database power, you can do tasks, you can manage track other things. Then they bring Notion to work. (00:57:24): Half our B2B customers coming from prior personal users, and most of them are using Notion for notes and talk in the first place. So pick. Well, at least we stumble upon a use case, a horizontal use case to give us a large top of funnel that help us grow our more verticalized enterprise use cases, and that's the reason where we ship a calendar product last year because which other category of software has 1 billion plus users? There's document notes, there's calendar, there's email, right? That's why we're also working on the email product right now.
turns.zh: 我自己倒不会另作他想，但我也不建议这么做。这是个问题。这个问题领域太大，很难形成最佳实践，但我可以分享一些对我们有参考意义的经验。关于Notion，我们一直致力于打造一个元工具，一个能填补我们软件不足的工具。我们最初把文档笔记当作一个典型应用场景，而这恰恰为我们带来了巨大的用户基础——每天有超过10亿人使用这个功能。这也推动了我们的业务增长。我们内部制定了一项名为B2C2B的战略。所有消费者、个人用户都以最简单的方式——笔记或文档共享——使用Notion。然后他们会发现："原来Notion还能做更多事。"比如它具备关系型数据库功能，还能管理任务、追踪其他事项。接着他们就把Notion带到了工作场景中。（00:57:24）我们半数B2B客户都来自原有的个人用户群体，而他们最初使用Notion时主要用于笔记和交流。所以关键在于，至少我们能从一个横向应用场景入手，吸引大量用户，从而为更垂直的企业级应用场景提供增长动能。这也是我们去年推出日历产品的初衷——毕竟哪个软件类别能拥有超过10亿用户？文档笔记、日历、邮件，哪个不行？这也是我们现在致力于邮件产品的核心逻辑。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: Yeah, man. Watch out, everyone. And then you mentioned AI and it's such a good point that AI is best when it has data. And the fact that you have all of this stuff already in there gives you a lot of really interesting opportunities to leverage AI.
turns.zh: 是啊，大伙要注意了。你提到的AI确实很关键，AI只有在有数据支持的情况下才能发挥最佳效能。而Notion已经积累了海量数据，这为我们应用AI技术提供了绝佳机遇。

turns.speaker: Ivan Zhao
turns.en: We definitely did not expect language model. It's such a gift for everybody building tools, right? Complete change the material you can work with. One realization, it's you have a surface area that people spend daily work with, especially during writing and managing your tasks and project. It's really easy to slice the language model writing AI capability into it. So that's the first part we built. That realization is AI is so good at reasoning and understanding and searching things, and we can do a much better job of finding and searching things if all the information are together. That's what we realized. AI is really good with bundled offerings. AI is really good with horizontal tools. So that's the second phase, we call it. The first product was our AI writer product. Second product is AI Q&A or connectors. Please look at all the information in Notion and give your answer. (00:59:18): And then we also need to work with the external connector because there's things that are living in Jira, living in Zendesk that other customers still rely on. So we need to build AI connectors. But more and more information coming back to the Notion core. I would say the third one, which is even more fascinating, it's for the longest time and it's still is one of the biggest weaknesses of building for Legos, it's hard to piece together. It's not everybody can put together a Lego set from scratch. There's always the builders and user with the Legos. But guess who is really good at piecing things together, assemble things? Especially things like since Sona 3.5. AI is so bad at writing code. Coding is just assembling things together. So now we're looking at holy shit, we spent the last five, six year building all those Lego blocks for knowledge work. If we're just putting AI coding agent on top of it, you can create any kind of knowledge, customer software, customer agent for whatever your vertical use cases you need. So that's the most fascinating approach for me, and we did not expect this at all.
turns.zh: 我们绝对没想到会有语言模型。这对所有开发工具的人来说都是一份厚礼，对吧？它彻底改变了你能使用的素材。突然意识到，你拥有一个人们日常工作时会频繁接触的界面——尤其是在写作、任务管理和项目协调时。将语言模型的写作能力融入其中实在轻而易举。这就是我们开发的第一阶段。我们意识到，AI在推理、理解和搜索方面表现出色，如果所有信息都能整合起来，我们的查找和搜索能力就能得到极大提升。这就是我们的核心洞察：AI擅长整合服务，擅长提供横向工具。这就是我们称之为第二阶段的阶段。首款产品是AI写作工具，第二款产品是AI问答或连接器。请查看Notion中的所有信息并给出答案。（00:59:18）此外，我们还需要与外部连接器协作，因为Jira、Zendesk等系统中仍有客户依赖的数据存储。为此，我们必须开发AI连接器。但越来越多的信息正回流至Notion核心平台。我想说，第三个突破更令人惊喜。这是构建积木式应用长期以来最大的痛点之一——难以拼合成完整的系统。并非所有人都能从零开始搭建积木套装，总有搭建者和使用者之分。但你猜谁最擅长拼合？尤其是自Sona 3.5版本以来，AI在编程方面表现糟糕。编程本质上就是将零件组合在一起。如今我们惊呼：过去五六年我们为知识工作搭建了所有积木块。若能在此基础上叠加AI编程代理，你就能创造出任意类型的知识产品、客户软件、客户代理，满足任何垂直应用场景需求。这对我来说是最迷人的突破，我们完全没有预料到。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: Thank you, AI. Is there anything else along the lines of building horizontal products and bundling that you think is interesting to share or important? Otherwise, I have one last question I want to ask you.
turns.zh: 感谢AI，还有其他关于构建横向产品和整合服务的有趣见解或重要观点吗？如果没有，我最后想问你一个问题。

turns.speaker: Ivan Zhao
turns.en: I think market is like waves. There's... Who said this? There's two-way to build business, bundling and bundling, right? There's too much of a zig and the zag. Actually, my favorite version of this is there's a classic Chinese literature called Romance of Three Kingdoms. It's great novel. It talked about the three kingdom era of China and the opening sentence of this novel, it's, "Empires long united must divide, long divided must unite." That has always been bundling, unbundling. It's one of my favorite book to read when I was a kid, but business works same way. When there's too much, you can see this. (01:01:29): It's like before computers, everything works on paper. Our knowledge work are done through papers is fully democratized medium. Then PC happens during the '80s. The first era is a piece there actually are so many applications. There's early database software, dBASE, it's quite famous. It started dBASE 2 because it gives them credibility. Oh, they have been stick around for some time. So that's the first unbundling phase of software computing. Then Microsoft bundled everything back into one suite in the '90s. Then the SaaS unbundled it. Now, we're at the tail end of SaaS. There's so many verticalized SaaS average company to use almost a hundred tools. It's madness. So there's more the market shifting towards more a bundling approach. And with AI and with the macro, so there's more value to be created through bundling, at least for now. The market could shift again. So understand this trend, I think, helpful to see should you build a vertical solution or should you build horizontal solution because it does different things.
turns.zh: 我认为市场就像波浪。有人说……谁说过这话？开展业务有两种方式：整合与拆分，对吧？市场波动太大，起起伏伏。其实我最喜欢的例子来自中国古典文学名著《三国演义》。这部伟大的小说讲述了中国三国时代的历史，其开篇语句是"合久必分，分久必合"。这始终是整合与拆分的循环。小时候我最爱读这本书，而商业运作的逻辑也如出一辙。当市场过度饱和时，就会出现整合与拆分的轮回。（01:01:29）就好比在计算机出现之前，一切都靠纸质文件运作。知识工作完全依赖纸质媒介实现民主化。80年代PC问世，首个时代诞生了众多应用程序，如著名的dBASE数据库软件。dBASE 2之所以能成功，是因为它树立了权威形象，证明了自身的持久价值。这是软件计算领域的首次拆分阶段。90年代微软将所有应用整合为Office套件。随后SaaS模式实现了再次拆分，如今我们正处在SaaS模式的尾声。许多垂直领域的SaaS产品让普通公司平均要使用近百种工具，这简直疯狂。因此市场正逐渐回归整合模式。借助人工智能和宏观趋势，整合模式目前仍能创造更多价值，但市场未来可能再度转向拆分阶段。理解这种趋势，有助于判断是构建垂直解决方案还是横向解决方案，因为两者侧重点不同。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: I love that story. Okay, so last question. Something that one of your early investors, Finn Barnes, suggested to ask you. I'm curious where this goes. There's this, and you've touched on this a number of times, just the way you think about Notion, it's almost like a philosophy of how to work and be versus just a productivity tool. And so I'm just curious how you think about the relationship between tools and human potential and humans and how we live in the world.
turns.zh: 我很喜欢这个故事。好，最后一个问题。早期投资者Finn Barnes建议我问你这个问题。我很好奇这会如何发展。你多次提及对Notion的看法，它几乎像是一种工作与生活理念，而不仅仅是生产力工具。我很好奇你如何看待工具与人类潜能、人类与世界生活之间的关系。

turns.speaker: Ivan Zhao
turns.en: The tools are extensions of us. That's why our office room named as timeless tools. They extend us a little bit. And once they extend us, once we shape them, once we bring them to world, they can come back to shape us. (01:03:29): One of my favorite quotes like the Marshall MacLean quotes, "We shape our tools. Then after, our tools shape us." I think that's probably too philosophical for building product or business, but there is a sense thinking what are you bringing to the world that will come back to bite you or shape you? And are you extending the part, the so-called good part of human nature, or are you extending the part that might be more zero-sum, might be more negative, right? (01:04:05): For me, what is Legos? Lego is creativity. Lego is beauty. Software to me feels like lacking both. It's definitely lacking a lot of creativity. It's so rigid. So I believe both are human nature that worth amplifying. You can build another business that amplifies a different part of human nature. There was Sequoia famously invests in seven sins or seven human natures of human because they're so powerful if you just latch onto them, you can create a business, you can create a product. But at least I prefer to amplify creativity and beauty in the domain of software. To me, that's aligned with my values and I think can at least shape the market, shape our user of our product towards the better part of themself.
turns.zh: 这些工具是我们自身的延伸。这就是为什么我们的办公室被命名为"永恒工具"。它们在某种程度上拓展了我们。当我们塑造它们、将它们推向世界后，它们又能反过来塑造我们。（01:03:29）：我最喜欢的引言之一是马歇尔·麦克伦（Marshall McLuhan）的话："我们塑造我们的工具，然后工具反过来塑造我们。" 我认为这对产品或商业来说可能太具哲学性了，但值得思考的是，你带入世界的东西会反过来影响你吗？你是在拓展人性中善良的一面，还是在放大可能带来零和博弈、更具负面影响的部分呢？（01:04:05）：对我来说，乐高是什么？乐高是创造力，是美感。但软件在我看来既缺乏创造力，又太过僵化。所以我认为这两种特质都值得放大人性。在软件领域，你可以打造另一个放大人性不同维度的业务。比如红杉资本（Sequoia）就投资过“七宗罪”（七种人性）项目，因为只要紧紧抓住这些特质，就能创造出商业模式和产品。但至少我更倾向于在软件领域放大创造力和美感。这与我的价值观相契合，我相信这至少能让市场朝着更积极的方向发展，让我们的产品用户变得更优秀。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: It must feel so good to have a product that is so aligned with the way you want to see the world and actually working and growing at this rate and scaling and becoming this, I don't know, part of the ether of the world.
turns.zh: 拥有一个与你理想的世界观如此契合的产品，并且能以这样的速度成长、扩展，成为世界不可或缺的一部分，这感觉一定很棒。

turns.speaker: Ivan Zhao
turns.en: It feels good. Yeah, it feels good that some of the most heartwarming thing is still it never gets old when you walk by coffee shop and see people using Notion. Oh, it feels good. And it feels good that we see people in our community can create a living selling Notion template, Notion apps, that they're not a software engineer. And going back to the original mission of when people create software, I think that's one of the most fulfilling thing, at least as a maker of tools can experience.
turns.zh: 确实很棒。最温暖人心的事情之一就是，当你路过咖啡店，看到人们在使用Notion时，那种感觉永远不会过时。这感觉真好。还有我们社区里有人通过销售Notion模板、Notion应用来谋生，他们甚至不是软件工程师。这让我回想起最初开发软件的初衷，我认为这至少是作为工具创造者最有成就感的部分之一。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: That last point, I think people don't realize, so people are making millions of dollars selling Notion templates on the internet like at Etsy and other places.
turns.zh: 最后一点，我觉得人们没有意识到，在Etsy等平台上，人们通过销售Notion模板已经赚了数百万美元。

turns.speaker: Ivan Zhao
turns.en: Consulting templates, yeah, and they're not programmers. I think I would say that's the heart of that because their domain expertise, they're YouTubers or creators. They have lifestyle brand. They know certain things but they're not makers of software. Then they can use Notion, package their workflows and expertise into Notion and templates and make limit with it. It's awesome, all that.
turns.zh: 咨询模板，没错，他们不是程序员。我认为这才是核心所在，因为他们的专业领域是YouTuber或创作者。他们有自己的生活品牌。他们了解某些领域，但并非软件开发者。他们可以使用Notion，将自己的工作流程和专业知识打包成Notion模板，并从中获利。这太棒了。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: Yeah, millions of dollars is it's crazy. Ivan, before we get to an abridged lightning round, I'm curious if there's anything else that you wanted to touch on think might be useful for folks to hear before we get to a very exciting lightning round.
turns.zh: 是啊，数百万美元，真是难以置信。伊万，在我们进入精简版闪电问答环节之前，我很好奇你是否还有其他想分享的见解，对听众可能有帮助的，在我们进入激动人心的闪电问答环节之前。

turns.speaker: Ivan Zhao
turns.en: I think people in tech, I wish more people look beyond tech to steal good ideas. It's like Tech Hacker News Twitter are so focused on the now and what's in front of it, what happened six months ago, versus humanity. If you just read books in other industry, you can look sideways. If you go back to history, there's a massive amount of patterns and shapes and trade-offs you can steal from and you can make what's in front of you much more interesting. You could give you... People figure out clever patterns in whatever domain in the past. You can just take in front of you. And I wish more people do that. I think it would be a very interesting way for product makers, business maker to solve the problem in front of them by stealing outside of from the domain of tech and business. So at least it's very inspiring, very useful for me personally.
turns.zh: 我觉得科技领域的人们，应该多看看科技之外的领域，借鉴好的创意。比如科技新闻、推特等平台的人们，总是过于关注当下和眼前的事物，却忽视了六个月前发生的事情，更忽视了人类的本质。如果你去阅读其他行业的书籍，你就能跳出固有思维。回顾历史，你会发现有大量可借鉴的模式、规律和权衡取舍，这些都能让眼前的问题变得更有趣。你可以从中汲取灵感……过去，人们在任何领域都能找到巧妙的模式，而这些模式如今都能为你所用。我希望更多人能这样做。我认为，这对于产品开发者和商业创新者来说，通过跨越科技和商业领域的界限来解决眼前的问题，将是一种非常有趣且有效的思路。所以至少对我个人而言，这非常鼓舞人心，也极具启发性。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: It makes me think of the quote, "Good artist copy. Great artists steal."
turns.zh: 这让我想起了那句话：“优秀的艺术家模仿。伟大的艺术家窃取。”

turns.speaker: Ivan Zhao
turns.en: Great artists steal, yeah. Well, Steve Jobs stole that from Picasso or something who stole from former artist probably.
turns.zh: 是啊，伟大的艺术家窃取创意。对吧，史蒂夫·乔布斯不就是从毕加索那里窃取灵感的吗？

turns.en: Well, this is actually an amazing segue to our very abridged lightning round. And the first question is... And by the way, welcome to the lightning round.
turns.zh: 嗯，这其实为我们简短的闪电问答环节提供了一个绝佳的过渡。首先，欢迎大家参与闪电问答环节。

turns.speaker: Ivan Zhao
turns.en: Oh, okay.
turns.zh: 哦，好的。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: The first question is just what are a couple of books that you find yourself recommending most to other people? Could be along the lines of what you just described or could just be generally.
turns.zh: 第一个问题是，你最常向他人推荐的书籍有哪些？可以沿着你刚刚描述的方向，也可以是其他方面的推荐。

turns.speaker: Ivan Zhao
turns.en: I think the domain that are interesting the most is the complex system domain. You can look up the term. I think more and more people talk about this, but thinking a system, complex system when all the different things merge together, it creates emergent properties. Talking about ants, talk about beads, talk about life itself. It's just so fascinating how do with few primitives, few Lego bricks, you can create a thing called life. That thing just, it's sugar for me. So I love reading in that domain. And this is really helpful for create product, at least a horizontal product because you're trying to channel the energy, smaller parts to create something that the sum is much larger than its parts.
turns.zh: 我觉得最有趣的领域是复杂系统领域。你可以查阅一下这个术语。越来越多的人在谈论这个话题，但当所有不同元素融合在一起时，就会产生新的特性。比如蚂蚁、珠子，以及生命本身。仅用几个基本元素、几块乐高积木就能创造出生命，这实在太神奇了。对我来说，这就是糖分般的享受。所以我喜欢阅读这个领域的书籍。这对产品设计非常有帮助，至少对于横向产品来说是这样，因为你试图汇聚各个部分的能量，创造出整体大于部分之和的产品。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: Is there a specific book that comes to mind or is it just generally that's a cool area?
turns.zh: 有没有具体的书名推荐？还是说只是对这个领域感兴趣？

turns.speaker: Ivan Zhao
turns.en: That's a cool area to your attention to.
turns.zh: 你特别关注这个领域。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: Next question. Do you have a favorite recent movie or TV show you've really enjoyed?
turns.zh: 下一个问题。你最近有没有特别喜欢的电影或电视剧？

turns.speaker: Ivan Zhao
turns.en: I like to watch old documentaries. Maybe this is another area or category too. There's quite a few on YouTube. People make really good documentary in the '80s, in the '70s. That's like all the old BBC ones, they're just excellent and they have a strong opinion in them. It's no longer just general education thing. They have a direction. They have a taste. Go look it up. Oh, yeah. One is a really good one to get started called Connections. I think it's called but the gentleman's name is Burke. It's about how different things from different domains inspire other domains, and usually he used 30 minutes or 60 minutes to chain together a bunch of connection of stories. It's really good for technologists to watch. Highly recommend.
turns.zh: 我喜欢看老纪录片。或许这也是一个值得关注的领域或类别。YouTube上有很多这类内容。80年代、70年代的BBC纪录片非常出色，不仅是通识教育内容，还带有强烈的观点。不再局限于基础知识，而是有明确的方向和品味。去查查看吧。对了，有一部叫《Connections》（《联结》）的纪录片，主持人是伯克（Burke）。它探讨不同领域的元素如何相互启发，通常用30分钟或60分钟的时间串联起一系列故事的关联。科技从业者绝对值得一看。强烈推荐。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: I feel a very consistent pattern throughout all of these answers and your entire conversation of just emerging properties, connections, Legos, building abstractions.
turns.zh: 我在所有这些回答和整个对话中都感受到一个非常一致的模式——不断涌现的特质、联系、积木式拼搭以及抽象概念的构建。

turns.en: Yeah, I think I did Enneagram. My Enneagram, it's 7 and 7. 7 is, it is actually perfect with what we just talking about. 7 is creative, finding connection, see the forest and tree. 8 is they call Challenger. It's like competitive AR optimizing. So true energy accessing me.
turns.zh: 是啊，我觉得我确实了解了九型人格。我的九型人格是7号和7号。7号特质与我们刚刚讨论的内容完美契合。7号善于创造，善于寻找联系，能看到森林与树木的全貌。8号被称为挑战者型。就像在竞争激烈的AR优化领域一样。这种能量真的深深触动了我。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: Oh, wow. It's all makes sense. I got to take this Enneagram. This comes up a bunch on this podcast.
turns.zh: 哦，哇。一切都说得通了。我得去了解一下九型人格。这话题在播客里经常被提起。

turns.speaker: Ivan Zhao
turns.en: Right, yeah.
turns.zh: 对，对。

turns.en: Final question. Do you have a life motto that you often think back to, that you often repeat in your head of just like when times are hard or just to keep going with something you're working on that you find useful?
turns.zh: 最后一个问题。你有没有一句人生格言，经常回想，或者反复默念的，比如在困难时期，或者坚持做某件事时觉得很有用的？

turns.speaker: Ivan Zhao
turns.en: I like to think things as a craft. You just make it better. Make for yourself. If it's unique enough for yourself and useful for others, things will follow.
turns.zh: 我喜欢把事情视为一门手艺。你只需不断改进，为自己而做。如果它对你个人独具价值，又能为他人带来益处，成功自然会随之而来。

turns.en: Ivan, thank you so much for being here. Two final questions, working folks find you online if they want to follow-up on anything, and then how can listeners be useful to you?
turns.zh: 伊万，非常感谢你今天的到来。最后两个问题：工作中的听众如果想进一步了解你，可以在哪里找到你？听众如何能为你提供帮助？

turns.en: Probably find on me on Twitter, Ivan Z-H-A-O. It's helpful give us feedback about Notion, about our product. That's the best help.
turns.zh: 可能在推特上找我，Ivan Z-H-A-O。关于Notion、我们的产品，任何反馈都很有帮助。

turns.en: What's the best way to do that? Is it like DM, Ivan, or is it-
turns.zh: 怎么联系你？是直接私信吗？

turns.speaker: Ivan Zhao
turns.en: Yeah, just DM me.
turns.zh: 对，直接私信我。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: Okay.
turns.zh: 好的。

turns.speaker: Ivan Zhao
turns.en: DM me. Yeah, that's probably the best way.
turns.zh: 私信我。嗯，这可能是最好的方式。

turns.en: Okay. Oh boy, here you go. And then you guys are hiring. Anything specific you're looking for? Anything people should know if they're like, "Oh shit, I want to go work here"?
turns.zh: 好的。哦，拜拜。接下来是招聘问题。有什么特别的要求吗？如果有人想来这里工作，应该注意什么？

turns.en: We're trying to hire misfits. So if you think you're a misfit, if you're exceptional at many things especially, you want to build Lego for software, you want to take interesting spin on AI with Lego for software, then DM me.
turns.zh: 我们正在寻找特立独行者。所以如果你觉得自己是个怪才，如果你在很多领域都特别出色，尤其是想用积木式拼搭来构建软件，或者想在AI领域用积木式拼搭做有趣的尝试，那就私信我。

turns.en: Amazing. Ivan, thank you so much for being here.
turns.zh: 太棒了。伊万，非常感谢你今天的到来。
